content.overview: Every share in a company having share capital must be distinguished by a distinctive number, except a share held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in that share in a depository's records.
content.glance: Every share in a company having share capital must be distinguished by a distinctive number, except a share held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in that share in a depository's records.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 45 (Numbering of shares). Every share in a company having share capital must be distinguished by its distinctive number. The section does not apply to a share held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in that share in the records of a depository under the Depositories Act, 1996. Apply the rule to shares held in certificated form and do not impose the physical distinctive-number requirement on dematerialised holdings covered by the exception.

sections.heading: General rule
sections.body: Every share in a company having share capital must be distinguished by its distinctive number.

sections.heading: Depository exception
sections.body: The section does not apply to a share held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in the share in a depository's records under the Depositories Act, 1996.

examples.title: Certificated shares numbered
examples.body: A company issues physical share certificates with distinctive numbers for each share. Section 45 is complied with.

examples.title: Demat shares
examples.body: Shares held in a demat account under the Depositories Act need not carry distinctive numbers under s. 45.

hypotheticals.question: Must dematerialised shares be numbered?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The proviso to s. 45 excludes shares held with a depository where the holder is entered as beneficial owner.

distinctions.title: Distinctive-number rule and dematerialised holdings
distinctions.left: Section 45 requires distinctive numbers for shares generally.
distinctions.right: The statutory exception applies to shares held through depository records by a recorded beneficial owner.

misconceptions.trap: All shares, including demat, must have distinctive numbers under s. 45.
misconceptions.correction: The proviso excludes dematerialised shares held through a depository.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Do all shares require a distinctive number under section 45?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The general rule applies, but shares held by a person recorded as beneficial owner in depository records are excepted.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does section 45 apply to dematerialised holdings?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The statutory exception applies where the holder of beneficial interest is recorded in the depository's records.

revisionPoints: Distinctive number is the general rule for shares.
The exception applies to shares whose beneficial owner is recorded in depository records.
Section 45 is a numbering rule, not a rule deciding beneficial ownership disputes.
